title: Realizing a prescribed monoidal incidence diagram by an inert relative limit cone
statement: Use the universe, nerve and coherent diagram conventions of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], monoidal infinity categories and inert maps of [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category], cocartesian edges of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], and joins and relative limits of [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone]. Let $p:\mathcal V^\otimes\to N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$ be a monoidal infinity category and $r\geq0$. Let $I_r$ be the finite category with objects $e_1,\ldots,e_r,v_0,\ldots,v_r$, nonidentity arrows $e_j\to v_{j-1},v_j$, and no others. Define $b_r:N(I_r)\to N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$ by $b_r(e_j)=[1]$, $b_r(v_i)=[0]$, with the two endpoint maps on the displayed arrows. Let $\bar b_r:\Delta^0\star N(I_r)\to N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$ have apex $[r]$; its legs are opposite to the inclusions of the consecutive edges and vertices into $[r]$. For every coherent diagram $f:N(I_r)\to\mathcal V^\otimes$ with $pf=b_r$ exactly, there exists $\bar f:\Delta^0\star N(I_r)\to\mathcal V^\otimes$ such that $\bar f|_{N(I_r)}=f$ and $p\bar f=\bar b_r$ exactly. Every apex leg is $p$-cocartesian, and $\bar f$ is a relative $p$-limit diagram. In particular, the endpoints, both arrows to a shared endpoint, and all their incidence triangles are retained with their specified restrictions. For $r=0$ one can take the apex to be $f(v_0)$ and its sole leg to be the identity. No colimit hypothesis is imposed on $\mathcal V$.
